text: Cast in the forges beneath the Hollow Citadel, this emblem bore the crest of an order that swore itself to the dungeon's first descent. The knights who wore it never came back up the same.
line: The order it served no longer has a name.

text: Soft-soled and worn smooth from ten thousand corridors, these boots belonged to a knight who valued survival over honor. The leather remembers every corridor it passed through.
line: They know the way down better than you do.

text: Grey as ash, wide as silence. The arcanists of the deep levels wore these to mark their rank — or perhaps their resignation. The brim still holds a faint charge, like a word held too long on the tongue.
line: A scholar's hat for a place that forgot scholarship.

text: The Arcane Emblem is not a weapon — it is a permission. Whoever shaped the dungeon's first wards carved these sigils to let certain things pass through. You are now one of those things.
line: Whatever shaped this place still lets it work.

text: Cut from a single sapphire by a mage who claimed she had seen the dungeon's end. She blinked past walls when the corridors closed. The gem still holds the fold in it, a wrinkle in distance.
line: Distance is a suggestion, not a rule.

text: Forged in the kiln-rooms beneath the Hollow Citadel, this emblem was carried by arcanists who never returned. The heat sealed into its face has no source anyone still living can name.
line: Still warm from fires long dead.

text: This emblem was etched with sigils that were never meant to be combined. Whoever combined them did so once, judging by the scorch pattern on the reverse side, and then not again.
line: Order and ruin share the same edge here.

text: The Rage Emblem was issued to berserkers who descended into the dungeon's lower strata before the first seals held. Those who wore it into battle were difficult to tell from the things they fought.
line: The line between fury and surrender is thinner than you think.

text: Azazel's name is pressed into this metal in a script that predates the dungeon itself. To hold it is to feel something notice you — not with malice, but with the patient attention of a trap that has been waiting a very long time.
line: He gave this away. Consider what that means.

text: The pages of this tome are made from something that grows in the dungeon's deepest chambers, pressed flat and dried until they resemble vellum. Pressed between them, still bright, are the spores that make them dangerous.
line: Roots remember what they once reached toward.

text: This tome was written in a language with no living speakers — though its practitioners were not always living when they spoke. The canopy it summons is not botanical. It is something that learned to grow in the absence of light.
line: What grows in the dark does not need the sun to reach.

text: Lighter than they look and quieter than they should be. These boots were made for corridors that punish noise, in a workshop no one has found since the dungeon's middle tiers closed off. The craftsmanship is precise in ways that feel deliberate.
line: Speed was always the better armor.

text: These carriers fold space at the ankle joint — a technique the mage-engineers of the Hollow Citadel called transient anchoring, and which the knights who borrowed them called cheating. Both descriptions are accurate.
line: The gap between here and there is negotiable.

text: The leather is cracked and heat-stained, and the brass fixtures glow faint orange no matter how long they sit in the dark. Whoever wore these last descended into the buried levels and came back with burns on their palms and something behind their eyes they never explained.
line: The flame buried here was not meant to stay buried.

text: Crude, heavy, and identical to ten thousand others the dungeon has swallowed. The locks it fits were never meant to be found, only to hold. The fact that you have the key says nothing good about who left it here.
line: Someone wanted this found. Be careful what you open.

text: The gauntlets remember every wall they've broken through. They're still looking for the next one.
line: The stone remembers the blow.

text: Woven from shadow that refused to disperse. The wearer doesn't disappear — the world simply forgets them.
line: Gone before you heard the footstep.

text: Carried by the last warden of a keep that no longer exists. The enemies still come.
line: Here. Face me.

text: Used to restrain something that shouldn't have been caught. Then something that shouldn't have been kept.
line: Hold.

text: The edge doesn't cut. It decides.
line: Not a killing blow. A sentence.

text: The warmth is wrong. It doesn't radiate outward — it pulls heat inward, toward something cold at the center.
line: It burns on the inside too.

text: Carved from the bedrock of the dungeon's lowest accessible tier. Whatever lived down there didn't need to move fast — it needed to not die. The stone remembers that priority.
line: Let them hit. It won't matter.

text: Shadow assassins who survived long enough learned to do more than vanish — they learned to vanish twice. The pendant is a reminder carved into copper: the dark comes back if you call it.
line: The shadow remembers where you were.

text: A mirror that reflects nothing visible. Hold it up and you see a room that takes longer to fade than it should, as though the pendant is negotiating with time on your behalf.
line: The moment stretches for those who know how to ask.

text: The mage-engineers called this the overclock. You fill every ability slot with something burning and then squeeze the crystal until everything that was waiting detonates at once. None of them survived testing. The crystal did.
line: Everything at once. That's the point.

text: Inscribed with the notation system of a dead school of magic — one obsessed not with the strength of spells but with their interval. They believed the gap between casts was where power was lost. They were right.
line: The pause is where you die. Close it.

text: An old contract. The terms are simple: you give something vital and something distant bleeds in proportion. The dungeon offered this deal to many people. Most accepted. Few read the second clause.
line: What you give, it gives back — somewhere else.

text: The weapon drinks what leaves the body at the moment of death. Not blood. The other thing. Whoever forged it didn't have a word for it in the language they were using, so they named the weapon instead.
line: They were going to die anyway.

text: Spun from thread that took longer to process than it should have — the weavers kept losing track of how much time had passed. They worked slowly. The wraps came out larger than the loom.
line: Everything you wear lasts longer down here.

text: Worn by a school of combat mages who believed rotation was the whole discipline. They trained until their spell cycling became involuntary. The belt kept count so they didn't have to.
line: Keep moving. The cooldown is the enemy.

text: The oath pressed into the metal is unambiguous: bleed and become stronger. The dungeon has seen a thousand versions of this deal. The ones who wore it longest were the ones who stayed closest to the edge.
line: Not dead yet. That's enough.

text: A shard of something that hummed in response to suffering — specifically, to ongoing suffering. Prolonged exposure to pain made it sing. The scholars who catalogued it didn't ask where it came from.
line: The longer it hurts, the harder it hits.

text: The stitching is wrong in a way that's hard to articulate — the robe seems to tighten slightly after each kill, as though it's drawing something in. It fits better than it should. That's probably the point.
line: Every death feeds the one still standing.

text: Plain iron, no inscription, no ornamentation. Knights who wore them said they felt the blows differently — not less painful, but more purposeful, as though the impact was going somewhere instead of just landing.
line: Hit until it means something.

text: Wearing it feels like giving something up. You are. The ring draws from the marrow, takes the buffer that keeps you upright, and trades it for something sharper. Some who wore it said they didn't miss what it took.
line: Less to lose. More to gain.

text: The void doesn't care what you spend — it cares that you spend something. This sigil reroutes the transaction. Your mana stays where it is. The cost comes from somewhere more personal.
line: The void accepts all currencies.

text: Grown in the dungeon's second tier by something that learned to grow inward instead of outward. The thorns face the wrong way. That was the design.
line: Touch me and find out.

text: A talisman from a tradition that believed speed was a form of honesty — you hit before the lie had time to form. The quicksilver inside never settles. Neither do the people who carry it for long.
line: First. Always first.
